summary: Cover-story lodash impersonation ships heavily obfuscated bundle with embedded AES-GCM primitive
details: @finaxis/common-js@0.3.6 declares itself with lodash identity markers (keywords `lodash`, `lodash-js`, and a README copied verbatim from lodash) but ships a single 662KB `javascript-obfuscator`-processed bundle at dist/common-js.js as its `main`. The build pipeline (`scripts.vendor:aes` and `scripts.obfuscate`) bundles @noble/ciphers AES-GCM into an inline IIFE and monkey-patches its `clean()` to tolerate undefined arrays — an atypical modification that expands what ciphertext inputs the decrypt path accepts. The obfuscator output uses a shuffled string array of roughly 15,183 entries with an inline decoder, hiding all constants (including any network destinations, keys, or command strings) from source inspection. The lodash cover-identity combined with embedded symmetric-decrypt capability and full-bundle string hiding is the loader/stealer shape rather than a utility library: a genuine lodash-family package has no reason to obscure its constants or ship an AES-GCM decrypt primitive.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
